correctness.rationale: For squarefree n, exact sigma multiplicativity yields the congruence restrictions. Even n=6P has d=6D, D=2 sigma(P)-3P>0 dividing P, and D modulo 3 forces odd number of additional primes. Exact extremal ratios exclude at most 10 extra primes and all deviations from the first ten at the 11-prime boundary; only q=97,103,109 remain and their exact D gcd P values exclude divisibility. Odd n has at most one prime 2 modulo 3 and its maximal 121-prime abundancy product is strictly less than 3. The checked standalone Python arithmetic certificate verifies all finite comparisons; it is not used to replace infinite reasoning.

value.rationale: The 2017 natural problem studied near-3-perfect single-redundant-divisor integers at small prime support, without a broad squarefree obstruction. This result establishes rigorous global necessary constraints: 15 total distinct prime factors minimum, 122 if odd, and strong prime-residue restrictions, with the entire first even abundancy-feasible support boundary excluded. The high odd bound follows from a structural p-adic sieve rather than an arbitrary finite search; it significantly narrows any search for squarefree examples. It does not claim existence or optimality.
